Prevention: Use certified healthy pest free seedlings.
Destroy all volunteer banana plants & old neglected plantations, which may harbour thrips.
Keep banana field free of host plants (pear squash, passionfruit, weeds).
Plant a trap crop hedge e.g.
Monitoring: Monitor with blue sticky traps (one per acre).
When thrips are found on sticky traps, examine 5 bunches per hectare every 2 weeks for thrips or thrips damage.
Look for small (1.5 mm), slender, brown insects that fall on a white paper upon tapping banana flower & fruit.
Look for silver speckling on upper side of outer banana fruit.
Look for fruit browning & deep longitudinal cracks that may appear as a result of thrips damage.
Consider direct control if the damage becomes excessive.
Direct Control: Azadirachtin 0.03% w/w (32% neem oil) based products.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear personnal protective equipment.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Follow instructions on product label on
Farmers to always seek technical advice.
No synthetic chemicals registered against thrips in banana.
